newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CSOB CUTS PRIME AND BASE RATES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CSOB CUTS PRIME AND BASE RATES.

text.p: Czech bank Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB) said on Wednesday it was cutting its prime lending rate by one full percentage point to 19 percent, effective immediately.
The bank, one of the country's four largest, said in a statement it was also lowering its base rate for up to one-year credits by one percentage point to 20 percent.
CSOB last changed its base rate on Tuesday, lowering it by one percentage point to 21 percent.

Czech banks have started lowering their rates after the Czech National Bank (CNB) began to ease restrictions on access to credit which were imposed in late May during a speculative attack on the Czech crown.
The country's largest commercial bank, Komercni Banka a.s., lowered its reference rate on Tuesday to 18.6 percent from 19.6 percent.
The CNB's Lombard rate has been at 50 percent since May 16 after the previous 14 percent, and the discount rate is 13 percent, up from 10.5 percent.

The central bank, however, began easing repo rates, lowering the one-week rate to 18.5 percent on Tuesday, down from 75 percent at its peak during the currency crisis which forced the central bank to float the crown on May 28.
